findings.title: KeyError risk when comparing authenticated user against missing 'sender' metadata
findings.body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch()`, the new check `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` accesses `integration.metadata["sender"]` with direct dict indexing instead of `.get()`. Elsewhere in the same file (`build_integration`), `sender` is explicitly treated as an optional field (`if state.get("sender"): integration["metadata"]["sender"] = state["sender"]`), implying integrations can legitimately exist without a `sender` key in metadata (e.g. integrations created before this feature shipped, or if the installation webhook that populates `sender` was never received/processed). For any such integration, this line will raise an unhandled `KeyError`, crashing the reinstall flow with a 500 error instead of showing the graceful 'Invalid installation request' page that the rest of this pipeline is designed to show.

findings.title: New user-mismatch check can be bypassed when Integration row does not yet exist
findings.body: When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist`, the code immediately returns `pipeline.next_step()` (line 482), completely skipping the newly added `github_authenticated_user` vs `sender` comparison further down. Since `sender` metadata appears to be populated by the asynchronous GitHub installation webhook rather than by this OAuth pipeline itself, if that webhook has not yet been processed when the user completes the OAuth dance (e.g. due to webhook delivery delay), the Integration row will not exist yet, this branch will be taken, and the newly-added authenticated-user validation will never run for that installation — defeating the security check this PR is meant to add for that race window.

findings.title: Unhandled exceptions from OAuth token exchange and user-info calls
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` (line 423) and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (line 434) are called without any exception handling. Only the subsequent `safe_urlread`/`parse_qsl` step is wrapped in a `try/except`. If GitHub's token endpoint is unreachable, times out, or `get_user_info` raises `ApiError` (e.g. GitHub API hiccup or rate limiting), the exception propagates unhandled and the user sees a generic 500 error instead of the intended 'could not verify installation' error page that this PR is supposed to guarantee for all failure cases.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the scenario it is named for
findings.body: The test was changed to add a second request using a hardcoded, deliberately different `state` value (`"ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`) than the one the pipeline actually signs (`"9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3"`, used everywhere else in this file). Because of the newly added `OAuthLoginView`, this mismatched state now causes the request to fail at the `state != pipeline.signature` check inside `OAuthLoginView.dispatch()`, never reaching `GitHubInstallation`/`build_integration()`, which is what actually raises the 'GitHub installation could not be found' error this test is supposed to validate (the GH `/app/installations/{id}` 404 stub set up at the top of the test is now never hit). The test now only re-validates the generic state-mismatch path (duplicating coverage already implied elsewhere) while silently dropping coverage for the original 404-from-GitHub scenario.

findings.title: No test coverage for failed OAuth token exchange
findings.body: The PR description explicitly calls out a third failure mode — GitHub failing to return a valid `access_token` for the supplied `code` (e.g. invalid or reused code) — handled by the `if "access_token" not in payload: return error(...)` branch. No test in the diff stubs a failing/empty token-exchange response to verify this path actually produces the expected error page, so this behavior is unverified.
